title: Agent Knowledge Graph Update Architecture
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI for EE Research
description: A vis-network graph of four agent levels (Personal Researcher, EECD Department, CSE, University of Minnesota), each with its own knowledge graph of Annual Budget, AI Usage Policy, and NSF Grant Award nodes. Three buttons send a Budget Information update top-down, an NSF Grant Award update bottom-up, and an AI Usage Policy Change from the CSE level in both directions, updating the matching node at each level it reaches.

learningObjectives: Explain how a knowledge update travels through a four-level agent hierarchy
Identify which agents originate an update and which only relay it, for top-down, bottom-up, and mid-level events

keyQuestions: Which agent originates this update, and which agents only relay it?
Why does the CSE agent send the AI policy change in two directions?
Why must every level update its own knowledge graph?
commonMisconceptions: A change at one level is automatically visible at every other level
assessmentOpportunities: Predict the order of node updates before pressing a button
Sketch a new event and state where it starts and which nodes change

controls: Budget Information: top-down update of the Annual Budget nodes
NSF Grant Award: bottom-up update of the NSF Grant Award nodes
AI Usage Policy Change: update starting at CSE and flowing up and down
Reset: return all nodes to their starting values
